action: Chapter title and agenda slides appear: fundamentals of rigging, then add-ons.
tool: slides
why: Orients the viewer; no Blender work yet.

action: A slide defines an armature as a set of bones, with a single bone drawn beside a full skeleton.
tool: slides
why: Explain what an armature is before using one.

action: In a plain scene with a few loose bones in Pose Mode, the artist rotates one bone and the chained bones below it follow, showing parent and child.
tool: Pose Mode, rotate bone
view: User Perspective, Pose Mode, properties editor showing the armature object tab
why: Teaches parent-child bone behaviour that Rigify relies on.
reader_equivalent: rotate_world(rig, bone, axis, degrees) on a parent bone; children follow

action: A slide shows a monster mesh with a bone chain, the Ctrl P Set Parent To menu, and a weight-paint heat map in blue to red.
tool: slides
why: Explains that weights decide how much each bone moves each vertex.

action: A slide titled add-ons shows Rigify's face rig as bones and drawn over a head from front and side.
tool: slides
why: Introduces Rigify as the first add-on.

action: With nothing but the default scene, the artist opens Add > Armature > Rigify Meta-Rigs and hovers Human; Animals and Basic are the other two entries.
tool: Add menu, Rigify Meta-Rigs
view: 3D viewport, User Perspective, Object Mode, 5.0.1 shown at bottom right
why: Shows where the Human metarig lives.

action: A second slide presents Auto-Rig Pro as a paid add-on with similar presets; the artist opens its store page then returns to slides.
tool: slides and browser
why: Mentions the alternative without using it.

action: The browser page for Auto-Rig Pro closes, a slide with its smart-rig panel remains, and the next section titled Posing Your Character begins.
tool: slides
why: Transition from rigging add-ons to posing guidance.

action: A posing slide pairs a stylised illustration with two photographs of real people in poses, under the heading about using references.
tool: slides
why: Reference matters before posing.

action: The slide lists what to look for in reference and the first bullet, line of action, appears while the artist points with the cursor.
tool: slides
why: First posing rule is line of action.

action: Slide with red hand-drawn curves over three reference photos shows the line of action running from head down through the supporting leg; the next bullet, find the balance, is added.
tool: slides with annotation pen
why: Find the single flowing curve of the pose first.

action: Green vertical lines are drawn over the same photos to mark where weight sits over the feet, with hips visibly shifted when weight is on one leg.
tool: slides with annotation pen
why: Check the pose is balanced over the feet.

action: Third and fourth bullets appear (push the pose past the reference, avoid symmetry) while the red and green overlay stays on the photos.
tool: slides
why: Stylised characters need exaggeration and broken symmetry.

action: The list now ends with avoid symmetry; the artist only talks over the unchanged slide.
tool: slides
why: Reinforce the symmetry rule.

action: Slide on contrapposto defines it as what makes a pose feel natural, shown with three standing reference photos.
tool: slides
why: Introduce contrapposto as the second posing rule.

action: Green arrows over the photos trace a line down the weight-bearing leg and two short lines across the shoulders and hips that tilt opposite ways.
tool: slides with annotation pen
why: Shows hips and shoulders tilting against each other.

action: Last posing slide on pushing poses with shape keys, with a before and after of a head profile; then a purple divider titled Rigging and Posing.
tool: slides
why: Shape keys can take a pose beyond what the rig reaches.

action: First Blender footage: the finished textured girl character in an A-pose is orbited front and side with Alt-drag, outliner shows a CH_ character collection with body, eyes, jaw, hair scalp and cloth entries.
tool: 3D viewport, Solid with textured colour, outliner
view: User Perspective, orbit then front view
why: Starting state before rigging: a neutral A-pose, standing upright.

action: In the outliner the artist drags the model collections into a new CH_..._model collection, leaving a CH_..._rig collection beside it.
tool: Outliner drag and drop
why: Split rig stuff from geometry before adding an armature.

action: With the rig collection selected and active, the artist opens Shift A > Armature and reaches Rigify Meta-Rigs.
tool: Add menu
why: Add the metarig into the rig collection.

action: From the Add > Armature > Rigify Meta-Rigs submenu the artist picks Human; a giant skeleton with a gold face rig appears around the character, arms and legs far off.
tool: Add > Armature > Rigify Meta-Rigs > Human
view: front then 3/4 perspective, Object Mode, metarig selected in rig collection
why: The template skeleton must be fitted to the mesh.

action: The artist stays in Object Mode, shows the N panel for the metarig (location 0, rotation 0, scale 1, dimensions about 1.58 by 0.285 by 1.98) and explains the object transform stays untouched; then switches to Edit Mode.
tool: Object Mode, N panel Item tab, Tab to Edit Mode
why: Fit bones in Edit Mode so the object transform remains identity.

action: In Edit Mode with all bones selected, the artist scales (S) and moves (G Y, G Z) the whole skeleton from front, side and perspective views until it matches the character's height, then turns on bones In Front.
tool: Edit Mode: S, G, Armature > Viewport Display > In Front
why: Match overall height first, then keep bones visible through the skin.
reader_equivalent: fit_metarig(meta, L) scales by crown.z / bone max z

action: Zoomed in on the head from the side, the artist selects the face bones with L (linked), selects the face bone inside the head bone, hides everything else with Shift H and the bone collections panel shows Face collections.
tool: Edit Mode: L select linked, Shift H hide unselected
why: Isolate face bones so the large skeleton does not get in the way.

action: From the front orthographic view the artist presses G Z on the pelvis bones, moves them evenly, then enables X-Axis Mirror in the tool options so one side drives the other.
tool: Edit Mode: G Z, tool options X-Axis Mirror
why: Work on one side only and keep both sides identical.
reader_equivalent: apply_map(...); mirror loop at the end of fit_metarig

action: Switching to Right orthographic (Numpad 3) the artist notices the spine is off, selects the spine bones with L, and moves them to follow the curve of the back.
tool: Edit Mode: Numpad 3, L, G
why: Spine should follow the body's side profile.

action: Still in side view, the artist box-selects single joints and moves them in Y so the spine and pelvis sit inside the torso and hip.
tool: Edit Mode: box select, G Y
why: Centre joints inside the volume.

action: At the leg, the artist drags the knee joint to the middle of the knee and the foot bone to the ankle, then places the toe bone on the ball of the foot, using G and G Y.
tool: Edit Mode: G, G Y
view: right orthographic, leg and foot zoomed
why: Knee at knee centre; foot bone where the foot hinges; toe at toe.

action: The heel bone is moved to the sole at floor level in side view, with a faint box showing the boot mesh behind it; an object transform of 3D cursor appears in the pivot menu.
tool: Edit Mode: G on heel.02.L
why: Foot roll pivot must sit on the floor under the heel.

action: From the front the artist switches pivot with the period menu (Median Point, Active Element, Bounding Box Center, 3D Cursor, Individual Origins), then S X scales the heel bone wider to match the shoe width.
tool: Edit Mode: period pivot pie, S X
why: Heel bone length follows the sole width.

action: Front orthographic then 3/4: the artist moves the shoulder (clavicle) bones along the collarbone line with G in X, Z and then Y, toggling X-ray with Alt Z to see the bone through the skin.
tool: Edit Mode: G, G Y, Alt Z X-ray
view: front orthographic then user perspective of neck and shoulder
why: Shoulder bone follows the collarbone and sits back in the shoulder volume.
reader_equivalent: ebs["shoulder.L"].head/tail from clavicle and shoulder landmarks

action: On the hand, the artist moves the palm bones to the middle of the palm and spreads fingers over finger shapes, working from top and perspective views with G and Alt Z.
tool: Edit Mode: G, Alt Z
view: front orthographic then perspective close on the hand
why: Palm bones belong in the centre of the palm; fingers inside finger volume.

action: The artist returns to Object Mode, selects the body, orbits the whole figure, and enters Edit Mode on the body mesh to find edge loops at each finger joint.
tool: Tab between Object and Edit Mode, body mesh
view: perspective, hand zoomed then whole body
why: Find the exact vertex ring at each knuckle to centre bones on.
reader_equivalent: band(body, ...) centre of vertices near knuckle

action: With a knuckle vertex loop selected in the body's Edit Mode the artist presses Shift S Cursor to Selected, goes back to the metarig, selects the finger joint and uses Shift S Selection to Cursor.
tool: Shift S pie: Cursor to Selected, Selection to Cursor
why: Snap each finger joint exactly to the centre of its knuckle ring.

action: Whole face bone block, seen at an angle: the artist selects all face bones, sees roughly where the forehead, temple and ear bones should go and begins aligning, with Shift Alt drags and G.
tool: Edit Mode: G with face bones
why: Face bones come pre-labelled by shape; fit them to the sculpted face.

action: The artist picks an ear bone and opens the snapping popover on the header, switching Snap To to Face Project (a Face Nearest option sits beside it) with Rotate and Scale checked.
tool: Header snapping popover: Face Project
why: Make bones stick to the skin so they follow the face contour.

action: Around the mouth, the artist moves lip and chin bones with G, cancels with Esc when wrong, and keeps pressing Alt Z; the warning is to move whole joints, not a single bone end.
tool: Edit Mode: G, Esc, Alt Z
view: front-3/4 perspective close on the mouth
why: Bones that only touch must stay together; Rigify errors otherwise.
reader_equivalent: move_joint(ebs, bone, end, new) moves every end at that point

action: Cheek and forehead bones are moved one by one near the cheek and above the eyebrow, with Alt Z to see the bone through the skin.
tool: Edit Mode: G, Alt Z
why: Cheek bones sit at cheek bulge; forehead bones high enough above brow.
reader_equivalent: apply_map on face bones; fix with move_joint

action: The eyebrow, nose-bridge and forehead bones are placed above the brows, hair is visible in the viewport; at the end the artist selects body and metarig and presses slash for local view.
tool: Edit Mode: G, Numpad slash local view
why: Hair clutters the view, so isolate body and rig.
reader_equivalent: edit_bones(meta); hide other objects with hide_set(True)

action: From right orthographic view with scale in millimetres, the artist box-selects nose bones and moves each down the bridge and to the nose tip along Y and Z with several G passes.
tool: Edit Mode: box select, G with grid shown in mm
why: Nose chain follows the bridge and stops at the top lip.

action: Side-orthographic zoom on the chin and jaw: the artist moves chin and jaw bones in several G passes, then turns snapping back on for the side jaw bones in a front-3/4 view and toggles X-ray.
tool: Edit Mode: G, snapping on for side bones, Alt Z
why: Chin at the front of the jaw, jaw bone at the hinge.

action: With only the head showing, the artist works on the eyelid ring: lid corners and middles are nudged, then Slash is pressed to bring the whole character back.
tool: Edit Mode: G, Alt drag, Slash local view
why: Lid bones should trace the eyelid edge corner to corner.

action: On the eye bone, the artist selects the head, presses Shift S Selection to Cursor so it sits at the centre of the eyeball sphere, then selects the tail and snaps that too; the white sphere is the eyeball mesh seen through the lid bones.
tool: Shift S: Selection to Cursor on eye.L head and tail
view: perspective, extreme close on the eye
why: Eye bone pivots from the centre of the eyeball.

action: Snapping is turned off and the eye bone tail is moved straight forward along Y (G Y) and a little in X so the bone points ahead, not at the lid.
tool: Edit Mode: G Y, G X, snapping off
view: perspective then pulled-out view of the whole face
why: Eye bone must point straight forward like a gaze.

action: With the metarig selected, the artist opens Object Data properties and finds the Rigify panel showing a note that the metarig uses the old face rig, with Upgrade Face Rig and Generate Rig buttons.
tool: Properties > Object Data > Rigify panel
view: front close on the face, face bones visible
why: Warns the face needs upgrading before generating.

action: The artist clicks Upgrade Face Rig; the warning vanishes and extra face bones appear on the face, which the artist inspects from 3/4.
tool: Rigify > Upgrade Face Rig
why: The new face rig adds bones such as jaw_master and others.

action: The artist reviews the placement of everything, then goes back to Object Mode and clicks Generate Rig; a status message at the bottom says the rig was generated and a new rig object appears with large circle controls around the feet.
tool: Rigify > Generate Rig
view: front then 3/4 from behind, metarig plus generated rig in outliner
why: Produce the control rig used to pose.

action: With the generated rig selected, the artist looks at it in front and 3/4 views and explains that Auto-Rig Pro would give the same result at this stage; Pose Mode is then entered.
tool: Object Mode to Pose Mode (Ctrl Tab)
why: Pose controls live in Pose Mode only; Edit Mode is left alone.

action: In Pose Mode, with the body shown and clothes hidden, the artist selects the character and rig and presses Slash to isolate them before binding.
tool: Slash local view, Ctrl Tab pose toggle
why: Remove clutter before parenting.

action: The N-panel Rigify tab shows Rig Main Properties (Neck Follow 0.5, Head Follow 0, Torso Parent Root) and Rig Layers buttons for Face, Torso, Fingers, Arm and Leg IK, FK and Tweak, Root; the artist says to switch layers off to reduce clutter.
tool: N panel Rigify tab, bone collection buttons
why: Hide unneeded control groups to see the rig more clearly.

action: In Pose Mode on the generated rig the artist scales a finger master control (f_index.01_master) with S, turning the Rig Main Properties Curvature, and the fingers curl wrongly sideways instead of toward the palm; scale values around 0.69 to 0.82 are shown in the header.
tool: Pose Mode: S on f_index.01_master.L
view: 3/4 close on left hand, N panel Item tab open
why: Test finger rolls: scaling a master should close the fist, not twist it.

action: Continuing the scale test, the artist reads the header scale readout (about 0.69 to 0.88) and shows the finger moves in a different direction than expected.
tool: Pose Mode: S on finger master
why: Prove the finger rig has a wrong hinge axis before fixing the metarig.
reader_equivalent: set pose scale then compare DEF-f_index.03.L tip direction

action: After pressing Esc the artist toggles Ctrl Tab to Object Mode and uses Slash to isolate the body, metarig and generated rig.
tool: Ctrl Tab, Slash local view
why: Return to the metarig and fix finger roll.

action: Metarig selected, Re-Generate Rig button shown in the Rigify panel; the artist enters Edit Mode on the finger chain and the N panel Item tab shows Head, Tail and Roll of the active bone (for example Roll near zero).
tool: Edit Mode on metarig, N panel Bone fields
why: Compare bone rolls across fingers before correcting.

action: The artist uses Ctrl R to roll selected finger bones interactively, checking each of the pinky and thumb chains until the local axes line up; the N panel roll values change per bone, for example about -142 degrees.
tool: Edit Mode: Ctrl R roll bones
why: Every finger bone should roll the same way so Z points to the palm.

action: Switching to right orthographic (Numpad 3) the artist points at the knee and says to keep a slight bend, then draws with the annotate tool and shows the finger bones are straight in line; he flags it as a problem.
tool: Annotate tool, Numpad 3
view: right orthographic of leg, then perspective of both hands
why: Straight chains confuse Rigify; keep a small bend.

action: Back in Edit Mode, the artist selects finger bones and uses Shift Alt W to rotate the chain, then says to scale finger bones on the x-axis.
tool: Edit Mode: select chain, scale on local axis
why: Straighten each finger onto a line.
reader_equivalent: apply_map finger joints to base.lerp(tip, t)

action: With transform orientation set to Normal, the artist presses S Z 0 Enter on each finger chain to flatten it along its normal Z, then R X to turn a thumb chain a few degrees; header shows Scale along normal Z and Rotation about 6.7 degrees along normal X.
tool: Edit Mode: S Z 0, R X, orientation Normal
why: Flatten the chain onto one plane so the hinge axis is clean.
reader_equivalent: pts[i] += back * length * 0.02 after straight line placement

action: Switching the pivot (period menu: Median Point, Active Element, Bounding Box Center, 3D Cursor, Individual Origins) the artist then selects the middle finger joints and moves them slightly in G Z so each chain has a little bend.
tool: Edit Mode: period pivot menu, G Z
why: Give Blender a bend direction so finger curl is predictable.

action: After nudging pinky and thumb joints with G and G Z, the artist returns to Object Mode, selects the metarig and clicks Re-Generate Rig in the Rigify panel.
tool: Object Mode, Rigify > Re-Generate Rig
why: Regenerate so the rig picks up the fixed fingers.

action: After regenerating, the artist drags a finger master through a fist and says to clear the pose with Alt R (rotation), Alt G (location) and Alt S (scale); the N panel shows scale Y about 0.45 and Rig Main Properties for the arm.
tool: Pose Mode: Alt R, Alt G, Alt S
why: Fast reset between tests.

action: The artist says bones should be handled in their own local space, switches the transform orientation from Normal to Local in the header, and shows the Rig Layers buttons in the N panel.
tool: Header Transform Orientation: Local
why: Pose rotations and scales need the bone's own axes.

action: With Local orientation the artist rotates a finger master about its X axis (R X, header reads 7.77 degrees about local X) and scales it down along Y until the fingers curl into a fist; this time the fingers curl toward the palm.
tool: Pose Mode: R X, S Y in Local orientation
why: Confirms the fixed finger rig curls the right way.

action: Full-body pose-mode view in front and side: the artist clears pose with Alt R, Alt G, Alt S, then rotates a foot control in side view (R X, about 15 degrees); the face is covered with widget shapes.
tool: Pose Mode: Alt R/G/S, R X
why: Quick check that the full rig responds before binding.

action: The artist zooms to the face where many control widgets sit over the head and explains that most objects use Surface Deform and subdivision so rig will slow; Cycles render properties with Simplify unchecked are visible.
tool: Properties > Render, Pose Mode
why: Slow viewport is the reason to turn Simplify on.

action: In Render Properties, the artist ticks Simplify and sets Viewport Max Subdivision to 0, then right-clicks the checkbox to add it to Quick Favorites (Q menu) so it toggles with Q.
tool: Properties > Render > Simplify, Q Quick Favorites
view: 3/4 close on face, Q popup visible
why: Speeds up posing; the artist leaves it on while posing.

action: In Weight Paint on the body, with the Options popover open: Mirror Vertex Groups on and X enabled, then Auto Normalize ticked; header reads Weight 1.000, Size 100 px, Strength 1.000, group DEF-lid.T.L selected.
tool: Weight Paint: Options popover X mirror, Auto Normalize
view: close on left eyelid in perspective
why: Painting a bone to 1 should strip others when Auto Normalize is on.

action: The artist moves a brow control and sees the top of the head move; he selects the group DEF-spine.006 (head), paints the skull in Weight Paint and red replaces blue above the brow; header Weight 1.000, Size 118 px, Strength 1.000.
tool: Weight Paint, group DEF-spine.006
why: Stop the forehead control dragging the skull top.
reader_equivalent: paint(body, "DEF-spine.006", lambda p: p.z > brow_z + margin)

action: Weight Paint on the upper eyelid group DEF-lid.T.L with a larger brush (Size 182 then 326 px, Weight 1.000, Strength 1.000): the artist paints inward from the lid edge, undoes a mistake with Ctrl Z, and switches to the second group to compare.
tool: Weight Paint: DEF-lid.T.L, F resize brush
view: front close on closed eye, overlays off
why: Tune the lid so it closes without folding.

action: Zoomed on the closed eyelid crease and brow group DEF-brow.B.L.004: Size about 320 px, Weight 1.000; the artist paints and views the eyelid with Alt Z, concluding that weights can get the lid shape but he wants a specific shape.
tool: Weight Paint, DEF-brow.B.L.004
view: front close on eye, X-ray toggles
why: Motivates switching to a corrective shape key for the lids.

action: In Pose Mode close on the left eye, the artist drags the upper lid control (lid.T.L.002) down along local Y with G Y until the lid is shut; the header shows the move distance in metres along local Y.
tool: Pose Mode: G Y on lid.T.L.002
view: front close-up, eye open then closed
why: Find the control position where the eye is fully shut.

action: With the lid control selected the artist opens the N panel, reads Location Y (about -0.02367 m), types a rounded value of -0.024 into the Y field and confirms; Rig Main Properties shows Eyelids Follow 1.000.
tool: N panel Item tab, Location Y field
why: Use a clean, known number for the driver.

action: With the body selected and the Object Data tab open, the artist clicks plus in Shape Keys; Blender adds Basis first and the artist says not to touch it because every other key is relative to it.
tool: Properties > Object Data > Shape Keys > plus
why: Basis must stay as the original shape.

action: A second shape key named eye_close is set to Value 1.000 (Range 0 to 1). In Sculpt Mode the artist uses the Grab brush (Size 354 px, Strength 0.400 in the header, X symmetry on) on the upper lid, then increases to 392 px and 460 px, pressing F to resize and G to nudge the lid edge.
tool: Sculpt Mode: Grab brush on eye_close key
view: left 3/4 close on the closed lid, X-ray off
why: Pull the lid into the shape it should close into, leaving the lower lid untouched.
reader_equivalent: write kb.data[i].co for lid vertices; mesh.shape_key_add(name="eye_close_L")

action: The artist presses Q to bring up Quick Favorites with Use Simplify checked, unchecks it so the subdivision shows again, and opens the Ctrl Tab mode pie (Object, Edit, Sculpt, Weight Paint, Texture Paint, Vertex Paint).
tool: Q Quick Favorites, Ctrl Tab mode pie
view: 3/4 close then pulled back to head
why: Re-enable subdivision to judge the finished lid shape.

action: Selecting the body and shape key, the artist shows the Value slider of eye_close with Range Min 0, Max 1, and explains a driver will control the key rather than the slider.
tool: Object Data > Shape Keys panel
view: front close with rig controls visible
why: The lid key must switch on automatically when the lid control moves.

action: Right-click on the shape key Value field, choose Add Driver; the popup defaults to Scripted Expression with a variable of type Single Property error; the artist changes Type to Averaged Value and picks the rig object from the object dropdown in the variable.
tool: Right-click Value > Add Driver, driver popover
view: front close, driver popup in the viewport corner
why: Link the key to the lid control's movement.

action: The Drivers Editor opens as a floating window; the artist selects the F-curve, sets the active key to Key Frame -0.024 with value 1.0 and the interpolation to Linear, and removes the second default point; the curve is a straight diagonal through 0.
tool: Drivers Editor (floating window), F-Curve tab
view: 3/4 close with Drivers Editor window over the viewport
why: Map the bone's Y travel to key value 0..1.

action: Testing the driver in Pose Mode: at rest Y location the eyelid stays open; the artist drags lid.T.L.002 down with G Y and the lid closes once it reaches the recorded value.
tool: Pose Mode: G Y on lid control
why: Verify the driver switches on at the right moment.
reader_equivalent: set lid location y 0, -0.012, -0.024; viewport_capture each

action: The artist notes the key was sculpted on both eyes so one lid control closes both; he drags the left lid control and both eyes close, showing the need to split the key per side.
tool: Pose Mode: G Y on lid.T.L.002
why: Left key must not move the right eye.
reader_equivalent: left_side / right_side vertex groups on each key

action: In Edit Mode the artist selects the body's centre line vertex loop (front orthographic, centimetres), creates vertex groups left_side and right_side, weight painting them: the right half is red and the left half blue with a blended band in the middle; Weight 0.500 with Auto Normalize is shown for the centre loop, then the key is renamed eye_close_L.
tool: Edit Mode vertex groups, Weight Paint view, Shape Key rename
view: front orthographic, then weight-paint view of whole body
why: Split the one corrective key into left and right halves.
reader_equivalent: vertex_groups.new(name="left_side"); add(ids,1.0 then 0.5 on the centre loop)

action: The key eye_close_L gets its Vertex Group field set to left_side; the artist then duplicates the key (it becomes eye_close_L.001), renames it for the right side and sets its Vertex Group to right_side.
tool: Shape Keys panel: Vertex Group field, Duplicate Shape Key
why: One key per eye, each limited to its own half.

action: The driver on the duplicated key is edited: the bone field points at lid.T.R.002 with Type Y Location and Space Local Space; the artist presses Update Dependencies, then tests by moving the right lid control with G Y.
tool: Driver popover: Bone lid.T.R.002, Y Location, Local Space, Update Dependencies
why: Right key follows the right lid control.

action: With the eye done, the artist pulls back to a full-body view, pokes at body and face controls with Shift Alt, and declares the width of the body done.
tool: Pose Mode, orbit with Shift Alt
why: Rig controls move the whole body; corrective keys are the only extras for now.

action: The artist selects the eye objects and the eyeball body in the outliner, adds the rig as active selection and presses Ctrl P, choosing Armature Deform > With Empty Groups instead of Automatic Weights.
tool: Ctrl P > Armature Deform > With Empty Groups
why: Eyes must not get automatic weights; empty groups are filled by hand.

action: Back in object view the artist toggles X-ray with Alt Z, checks the eyes have picked up the rig's vertex groups with no weight, and says each part gets groups for every deform bone but no assignment.
tool: Object Mode, Properties > Object Data > Vertex Groups
why: Empty groups let the weights be assigned deliberately.

action: With an eyeball selected in Edit Mode the artist sets the search box to eye, picks DEF-eye.L in the Vertex Groups list, makes sure Weight reads 1.000 and presses Assign for all vertices, repeating for the cornea and the right eye.
tool: Edit Mode: Vertex Groups panel Assign, Weight 1.0
why: Eyeball moves entirely with its eye bone.

action: In Edit Mode on the jaw object (teeth and gums) the artist uses right orthographic (Numpad 3) and Ctrl L to select the linked upper teeth island, searches the groups for teeth and picks DEF-teeth.T.
tool: Edit Mode: Ctrl L, vertex group search "teeth"
view: right orthographic in millimetres, X-ray on
why: Select only the upper teeth for their own group.

action: The artist presses Assign with Weight 1.000 for the upper teeth, then Ctrl I inverts the selection and, with the tongue selected out of it, assigns the lower teeth and gums to DEF-teeth.B.
tool: Edit Mode: Assign, Ctrl I
why: Upper and lower jaw parts follow different bones.

action: In Weight Paint on the tongue, with the armature bones selected, the Weights menu shows Assign Automatic from Bones, which weights only the groups matching the currently selected bones; the tongue bones are visible with a gradient from red to blue on the tongue.
tool: Weight Paint: Weights > Assign Automatic from Bones
view: 3/4 close on tongue with rig bones shown
why: Auto-weights limited to the tongue bones only.
reader_equivalent: blend three tongue groups linearly along tongue length

action: After the tongue, the artist pulls back and clicks the eyebrow curves (surface curves attached to the brow scalp) saying not to parent curves but the scalp meshes; the Surface field in properties points at the brow scalp mesh.
tool: Object Data of hair curves, outliner
why: Hair curves follow their scalp through the Surface link, so parent the scalp.
reader_equivalent: part.parent = rig on scalp meshes only

action: The scalp meshes are multi-selected in the outliner (brow, hair, lashes, ponytail) with the rig, and Ctrl P > With Empty Groups is chosen; then the main hair scalp is selected and, in Edit Mode, all its vertices are assigned to one group.
tool: Ctrl P > With Empty Groups; Edit Mode Assign
view: 3/4 on head, X-ray, side view of scalp
why: Scalps follow the head rigidly.

action: Weight check: the artist selects the head control, confirms the main hair follows, then selects the body and the eyebrow and lash scalps for copying weights; the vertex groups of the body list DEF-spine and others.
tool: Pose Mode test, Object Mode selection
why: Hair scalp follows head; brows and lashes need real body weights.

action: With the body active and the brow scalp selected, the artist opens Weight Paint and Weights > Transfer Weights; the redo panel shows Data Type Vertex Group(s), Vertex Mapping set to Nearest Face Interpolated, and Source Layers Selection switched to By Name.
tool: Weight Paint > Weights > Transfer Weights
view: 3/4 close on face, weight paint mode
why: Copy the skin weights onto brows and lashes.
reader_equivalent: copy_weights(body, scalp) using DATA_TRANSFER POLYINTERP_NEAREST by name

action: After the transfer, the artist moves the upper lid control with G Y and the lash scalp closes with the lid instead of staying behind.
tool: Pose Mode: G Y on lid control
view: front 3/4 close on eye with lashes
why: Verify lashes and brows follow lids.
reader_equivalent: rotate or move lid control, then viewport_capture

action: Zoomed out, the head control is moved in all views and the clothes, skirt, shirt and necklace are noted as not yet bound; shirt, skirt and boots sit in empty space away from the rig when the root control is dragged with G.
tool: Pose Mode: G on root control
why: Shows which parts are not bound yet.

action: The artist binds the shirt with Ctrl P With Empty Groups, copies the body weights onto it with Transfer Weights (by name, as for the lashes), turns Simplify on, and then rotates the chest control (header about 17 degrees) to check the shirt follows.
tool: Ctrl P With Empty Groups, Weights > Transfer Weights, R on chest
why: Close-fitting cloth takes the body weights so it moves exactly like the skin under it.

action: The artist lowers the main hair Geometry Nodes modifier Viewport Amount to 0.02 so the hair is light, selects the head control and rotates it about 17 degrees to confirm, and hides all the hair scalps in the outliner.
tool: Modifiers > GeometryNodes Viewport Amount, R on head
why: Keep viewport fast while posing.

action: With the shirt posed, the artist notes it deforms nicely, then switches to the boots and skirt, looking at boot detail and the Subdivision modifier (Catmull-Clark, Levels Viewport 1, Render 2) on the skirt.
tool: Object Mode, Modifiers panel
why: Layered boots and skirt are poor candidates for automatic weights.

action: The artist adds a cube, scales it to cover the character and renames it with F2; he copies the shoe's name from its rename field (Ctrl C) and pastes it into the cube name to make GEO_..._shoe_rig_helper.
tool: Add > Mesh > Cube, F2 rename, Ctrl C / Ctrl V
view: front full body, cube far larger than the character
why: Create the helper proxy for the boot.

action: The name field fills in GEO_..._shoe_rig_helper, the artist presses Enter, and drags the cube in the outliner into a new CH_..._rig_helpers collection.
tool: F2 rename, Outliner drag
view: front view with oversized cube, outliner
why: Keep helper proxies in their own collection.

action: In Edit Mode the artist cuts extra loops into the boot-shaped helper with Ctrl R, then switches to Sculpt Mode with the Grab brush (Size about 322 to 482 px, Strength 0.400) and smooths the shape (header field reads 0.400) so the proxy hugs the boot just outside it.
tool: Edit Mode: Ctrl R loop cut; Sculpt Mode: Grab and Smooth
view: low 3/4 view of the boot beside the helper (white, shoe-shaped)
why: The helper must wrap the boot without poking through it.
reader_equivalent: follow_helper(part, helper, rig); helper built by projecting verts to the part's surface plus offset

action: The helper has a Mirror modifier above an Armature modifier (object rig); the artist selects helper then rig, uses Ctrl P > With Automatic Weights, and checks the rig affects the helper in a front view with Esc, Tab and rotation controls.
tool: Ctrl P > With Automatic Weights; modifiers panel
view: front low view, both white helper boots visible
why: The helper alone is auto-weighted; only it follows the rig by weights.

action: On the real boot (GEO_..._shoe) with modifiers Mirror, Armature, SurfaceDeform and Subdivision, the artist picks the helper in the SurfaceDeform Target field; Interpolation Falloff 4.000, Strength 1.00 shown. He then toggles Simplify in the Q menu.
tool: Modifier SurfaceDeform: Target, Falloff, Strength
view: front low view, helper shown as wire cage over boots
why: Surface Deform lets the high-poly boot follow the helper.

action: The artist says to keep Simplify on with the lowest subdivision before binding Surface Deform, clicks Bind (button turns to Unbind), and Render Properties are shown with Sampling for Cycles.
tool: SurfaceDeform > Bind, Render Properties Simplify
why: Binding with active subdivision errors.

action: In Pose Mode the artist grabs the foot IK control and rotates and moves it; boots with the helper wireframe deform together cleanly, which the artist says automatic weights could not do.
tool: Pose Mode: G and R on foot_ik.L
why: Check boot follows the foot, ankle and shin.

action: The helper is hidden in the viewport and render through the outliner toggles; the artist hides the skirt helper object in the same way and says helpers stay out of renders.
tool: Outliner: eye and camera toggles on the helper
why: Helpers are scaffolding and must not render.

action: Sped up four times, the artist adds a cube for the skirt helper, scales it with S and moves it with G Z in front view into a flat skirt shape, rotates around to align it, and loops cuts it; the object sits in the rig_helpers collection with a Mirror modifier.
tool: Edit Mode: S, G Z, loop cuts; Add Cube
view: front orthographic then 3/4 from the left
why: Skirt proxy models the shape of the skirt just outside.
reader_equivalent: build helper as scaled cube, SIMPLE subdivision, project verts outward

action: With the finished skirt helper shown as a wire cage over the skirt (Viewport Display As Wire), the artist selects helper then rig and presses Ctrl P with Automatic Weights, then moves the foot control to confirm the helper follows.
tool: Ctrl P > With Automatic Weights
view: front low view of the skirt
why: Same recipe as the boots.

action: In Pose Mode the artist rotates the hips control about 17 to 22 degrees (R Z) and the skirt swings smoothly; a small amount of clipping through a raised leg is visible and noted.
tool: Pose Mode: R Z on hips control
view: front and 3/4 of skirt and thighs
why: Test the skirt deforms without spikes; find clipping.

action: Back in Pose Mode the artist raises a foot control (G, with Shift Alt orbit) and the skirt still clips with the thigh; the skirt now shows Armature, SurfaceDeform (Bound, Unbind button) and Subdivision, and the artist says he will sculpt the skirt outward.
tool: Pose Mode: G on foot control; SurfaceDeform panel
view: front 3/4 on skirt, then front full figure
why: Clipping is fixed by reshaping the skirt, not the weights.
reader_equivalent: unbind SurfaceDeform, edit the skirt, bind again

action: With the body selected the artist shows the Modifier tab: Armature then Subdivision (Catmull-Clark, Levels Viewport 1, Render 2), says parts under the clothes can be hidden so they do not clip.
tool: Modifiers panel on body
why: Introduce the Mask modifier for hiding skin.

action: The artist tests the chest control (R) bending the shirt, then clicks the necklace object and says the necklace gets the same helper treatment as the skirt; the skirt helper has Mirror and Armature modifiers and shows as a wire cage.
tool: Pose Mode R on chest; select necklace
why: Same recipe for the necklace as for boots and skirt.

action: The artist says the rigging is done and tests poses; he selects the rig and moves a foot control (G) with local view of the whole character; the necklace object shows no modifiers yet.
tool: Pose Mode: G on foot control
view: front full body, helper collections visible
why: Quick test of the rig after all binds.

action: The artist hides the helper collection and poses with legs and the hips control (Z and R keys), then selects the body and finds a Modifier stack of Armature, Mask, Subdivision; he recommends starting with the bare body.
tool: Pose Mode: G, R; body modifiers Armature, Mask, Subdivision
why: Pose bare body first; clothes can wait.
reader_equivalent: m.show_viewport = False on Mask while posing bare body

action: Local view then the Mask modifier's viewport toggle is clicked off; the clothes and underwear regions vanish from the mask and the whole bare body appears with the control rig on top.
tool: Modifier panel: Mask viewport toggle off, Slash local view
view: front and 3/4 full body, bare body
why: See the bare body to judge the pose silhouette.

action: The artist switches the viewport editor to the Asset Browser (editor type menu), chooses Current File in the library list and the Unassigned catalog is empty; this is where pose assets will appear.
tool: Editor type > Asset Browser, Current File
why: Store the pose where it can be reapplied later.
reader_equivalent: key the pose on its own frame (e.g. 101)

action: After posing, the artist creates a pose asset in the Asset Browser; a camera appears in the scene and a thumbnail named by the artist shows under the Current File Unassigned catalog; the hovered tooltip says Asset Library: Current File.
tool: Pose Mode, Asset Browser > Asset > Create Pose Asset
view: 3/4 view with Asset Browser beside it
why: Pose preview thumbnail needs a camera.
reader_equivalent: keyframe all control bones on a pose frame

action: The artist states to store at least two poses, and the viewport changes to a wide 3/4 with a camera in view; he asks to clean up the rig before posing then finishes the chapter on a title card.
tool: Pose Mode, Asset Browser
view: 3/4 view, camera frame appears as a black triangle
why: At least two presentation poses are required.
reader_equivalent: keyframes on frames 101 and 102; turnaround_sheet each

action: Closing slides ask the viewer for a review, then the next chapter starts; no further Blender work.
tool: slides
why: End of the chapter.
